name: used_car_check
description: Use when the owner is buying or selling a used car, or asks whether fault codes were cleared recently to hide a problem.
instructions: Call read_inspection {} once: it reads MIL, stored / pending / permanent codes, readiness, the distance since codes were cleared, the freeze frame, the in-use counters and the VIN, and assesses them.
The first line is "Verdict: <pass|caution|fail> (score N/100)"; each further line is "<status>: <check> — <detail>" with status pass, warn, fail or info.
When stored or permanent codes are listed, look them up with read_dtcs_detail before you explain what they mean for a buyer.
Say plainly that this screens the engine / emissions ECU only: it is not a mechanical, body or accident-history inspection.
interpret: Verdict fail: a stored or permanent code or the MIL is on. Permanent codes cannot be cleared by a tool or a battery pull: they mean a current emissions fault.
Verdict caution: pending codes (intermittent, not yet confirmed), a possible recent code clear or recently reset in-use counters.
"Possible recent code clear" needs three or more monitors not ready, no stored codes and at most 80 km since codes were cleared: advise a re-check after a full drive cycle before buying.
Monitors not ready on their own are not proof of tampering: a recent battery disconnect does the same.
Fewer than 50 OBD monitoring cycles in the in-use counters (IUPR) means the OBD memory looks recently cleared even when readiness has been driven back to complete.
Verdict pass means the emissions ECU shows nothing suspicious right now; it never proves the car is sound.
